subject: Dedicated pool sizing proposal and surge clause for ScarlettAI – follow-up
messages:
From: Evan Liu <evan.liu@scarlettai.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@scarlettai.com>, Scarlett AI Procurement <procurement@scarlettai.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — Q3 forecast + APAC edge requirement

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Scarlett AI is ramping faster than we modelled and we need to lock a predictable dedicated lane for inference for the next two quarters. High-level: we expect 120M monthly tokens by July with 30% of traffic requiring APAC edge nodes (low-latency inference for Singapore/Tokyo).

Key asks:
- Dedicated pool (reserved) with predictable throughput and a 2x burst buffer for peak days.
- Regional pools: US primary, EU standby for failover, APAC edge (Singapore) with smaller nodes but strict p99 latency targets.
- Price and SLA options for a 12-month commitment, plus a surge clause for one-off marketing spikes.

Attached a forecast CSV and a quick diagram of our topology. Can you share a sizing proposal + draft SOW and any procurement steps we should prepare for?

Evan
Evan Liu
Head of Platform, Scarlett AI
Attachment: scarlettai_usage_forecast_Q3-Q4.csv (csv)
Attachment: scarlettai_requirements_diagram_v2.png (png)
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@scarlettai.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@scarlettai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — Q3 forecast + APAC edge requirement

Evan — thanks for the clear ask and the files. Looping in Karthik (capacity planning) and Marissa (commercial) to scope sizing and SOW. Initial questions so we size conservatively:

- Is the 120M token/month steady-state or front-loaded in Q3? (CSV looks weekly but want to confirm peak day shape)
- For APAC edge, do you need region-local KV cache (stateful session affinity) or just single-region model execution with low latency?
- Any regulatory constraints in EU (data residency) that would force local inference vs. routing?

Plan: Karthik will propose a tri-region sizing matrix (sustained baseline + 2x burst buffer + recommended node types). Marissa will follow with contract/term options and a suggested surge clause template. We aim to send a packaged proposal by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Mina
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Liu <evan.liu@scarlettai.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@scarlettai.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — Q3 forecast + APAC edge requirement

Mina / team / Evan — put a first-pass sizing below after ingesting the CSV and running the traffic-shape assumptions. This is a conservative starting point; we can tighten after your confirmation on traffic skew.

Overview (baseline / burst buffer / recommended node types):
- US (primary): 60M tokens/month sustained -> baseline 8 x A100-80GB-equivalent nodes (continuous serving), burst buffer: +8 nodes available via reserved ramp (2x).
- EU (standby/failover): 30M tokens/month steady -> baseline 4 x A100-equivalent nodes, burst buffer +4. Note: if EU residency required, promote to active routing layer.
- APAC (edge Singapore): 30M tokens/month but latency-sensitive -> baseline 6 x 40GB T4-equivalent small nodes (low-latency config), burst buffer +6. Suggest deploying a lightweight KV cache per node for session affinity.

SLA & surge clause (proposal):
- Baseline SLO: 99th p99 token latency target per-region (US/EU/APAC) with committed throughput.
- Burst window: customers can initiate up to 2x baseline sustained for up to 72 hours (one free surge per quarter) subject to capacity availability — beyond that, charge at a surge unit rate (per-node-hour).
- Pre-warm notice: for marketing spikes >3x baseline, request 48h notice to guarantee buffer availability; shorter notice accommodated with a premium.

Costing notes (rough):
- Baseline monthly reserved node equivalent: estimate $XXXk/mo (detailed cost sheet attached in final PDF).
- Burst pricing: incremental per-node-hour to cover capacity and priority routing.

Operational items required from Scarlett:
1) Confirm token shaping (daily/weekly peaks).
2) Provide any EU data residency constraints.
3) Define acceptable failover latency SLA for EU -> US routing.

I'll convert this to a sizing matrix + SOW draft for Marissa to review. If you want a tighter APAC latency plan, we can run a mini benchmark with your traffic sample (takes ~48h).

— Karthik
Senior Capacity Planner, Redwood Inference
Attachment: initial_capacity_terms_draft.docx (docx)
From: Evan Liu <evan.liu@scarlettai.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@scarlettai.com>, Scarlett AI Procurement <procurement@scarlettai.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — Q3 forecast + APAC edge requirement

Thanks Karthik — this is exactly the level of detail we need. A few quick clarifications:

- The 120M token/month is our expected average for Q3 but with several product launches it can front-load; we'll confirm daily shape by Monday.
- For APAC edge we do want local KV cache to preserve conversational context within region.
- EU residency: we need logs and any PII processed to stay in-region; so if failover routes to US it must be opt-in only.

Please proceed to the SOW draft + pricing breakout. Procurement will review the surge clause and revert with any legal redlines.

Evan
Evan Liu
Head of Platform, Scarlett AI
